question.prompt:
Figures \(I,\) \(II\) and \(III\) are squares. The perimeter of \(I\) is \(12\) and the perimeter of \(II\) is \(24.\) The perimeter of \(III\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q06_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
A square has four equal sides, so divide its perimeter by \(4\) to find one side. Squares \(I\) and \(II\) have side lengths
\[
12\div4=3\qquad\text{and}\qquad24\div4=6.
\]
The right side of square \(III\) consists of a side of square \(I\) followed by a side of square \(II\), with no gap or overlap. Thus square \(III\) has side length \(3+6=9\). Its perimeter is
\[
4\times9=\boxed{36},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Find and add the side lengths
